title: When Do Larger Batches Help Scale LLM Reinforcement Learning?
abstract: arXiv:2608.29296v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Larger batches reduce the variance of stochastic gradients per update and are therefore often expected to accelerate training. Yet whether this statistical benefit translates into lower wall-clock time-to-target remains unclear, because each update consumes more samples and may take longer to execute. We study this tradeoff in reinforcement learning for large language models. We separate its algorithmic and systems effects by comparing learning and execution along their natural axes. At the algorithmic level, we compare configurations at equal cumulative sample counts while retuning batch-dependent hyperparameters. Over a bounded range of batch sizes, this procedure yields an approximately batch-size-invariant family whose members follow similar sample-indexed learning trajectories. translated_title: 大批次何时有助于扩展大语言模型强化学习？
translated_abstract: 更大的批次可以降低每次更新中随机梯度的方差，因此通常被认为能够加速训练。然而，这种统计上的收益是否能转化为更低的实际训练时间（达到目标性能所需的墙上时钟时间）仍不清楚，因为每次更新会消耗更多样本，且执行时间可能更长。我们在大语言模型的强化学习中研究这一权衡。我们通过沿学习与执行的自然维度分别进行比较，将算法效应与系统效应分离。在算法层面，我们在相同累计样本数下比较不同配置，同时重新调整与批次大小相关的超参数。在一定的批次大小范围内，这一方法产生了一个近似批次大小不变的配置族，其成员遵循相似的按样本索引的学习轨迹。在系统层面，我们利用了轨迹生成与训练之间的计算不对称性：自回归生成通常受内存带宽限制……
tldr: 该论文将大批次训练在大语言模型强化学习中的算法效应与系统效应分离，发现一定范围内批次大小对学习轨迹影响甚微，而实际加速主要来自利用轨迹生成与训练之间的计算不对称性来优化系统执行。
en_tdlr: This paper disentangles the algorithmic and systems effects of larger batches in LLM reinforcement learning, showing that learning trajectories are approximately batch-size-invariant over a bounded range, while wall-clock speedups stem from exploiting the computational asymmetry between rollout generation and training.
